extracted.intended_audience: communication scholars, journalism researchers, and news editors/industry professionals
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical research study investigating whether online audience metrics (clicks/page views) influence journalists' news selection, and how the use of these metrics relates to professional journalistic norms; uses mixed methods on five Dutch national newspapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience clicks / page views as a selection metric
rubrics_metrics.description: On newspaper websites, journalists can observe the preferences of the audience in unprecedented detail and for low costs, based on the audience clicks (i.e. page views) for specific news articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article's cross-lagged analysis covering 6 months found that storylines of the most-viewed articles were more likely to receive attention in subsequent reporting, which indicates that audience clicks affect news selection. This implies clicks/page views function as an empirical input or criterion that can shape what receives follow-up coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional norms in news selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors consider the use of audience preference information for news selection to conflict with professional norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews with editors indicate a perceived conflict between using audience metrics to guide story choice and established journalistic norms; the paper emphasizes the discrepancy between normative ideals (what editors say should guide selection) and observed behaviors (what metrics appear to influence selection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Storyline prominence measured by subsequent reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Storylines of the most-viewed articles were more likely to receive attention in subsequent reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study treats increased attention in later reporting as a measure of selection/promotion: prominence of a storyline (operationalized as subsequent coverage) is both an outcome and an indicator of selection decisions influenced by audience metrics.
